title: Microsoft Purview DLP: quarantine files in SharePoint and OneDrive
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, E5 licensing statement, quarantine behaviour and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should extend the policy path to the action and reconcile checklist controls and the tenant-switch caveat with the controls table.

claims.claim: File quarantine is a Microsoft Purview DLP policy action for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: File quarantine is a DLP policy action for SharePoint and OneDrive locations.

claims.claim: A matching file is removed from its original location.
claims.quote: Removed from the original SharePoint or OneDrive location.

claims.claim: A matching file is moved to an admin-defined SharePoint quarantine site.
claims.quote: Moved to an admin-defined quarantine site in SharePoint.

claims.claim: A tombstone text file replaces the quarantined file at its original location.
claims.quote: Replaced at the original location with a tombstone text file that contains an admin-configured message.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Quarantine removes access from everyone, including the file owner.
claims.quote: It removes access from everyone, including the file owner.

claims.claim: Quarantine applies to files created or modified after the policy with the action is turned on.
claims.quote: The quarantine action only applies to files that are created or modified after the policy with the quarantine action is turned on.

claims.claim: Pre-existing files are not evaluated for quarantine, subject to the first-time on-demand classification case stated under Scope.
claims.quote: Files that existed before the policy was activated aren't evaluated for the quarantine action.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes the existing-file behaviour as deliberate because reversing mass quarantine would require manual restore.
claims.quote: This design prevents a situation where a broadly scoped policy accidentally quarantines a large number of existing files, which would be difficult to reverse because file restore is a manual process.

claims.claim: Designating a SharePoint quarantine site automatically excludes its contents from DLP rule evaluation.
claims.quote: Once you designate a SharePoint site as the quarantine location, the contents of that site are automatically excluded from DLP rule evaluation.

claims.claim: Learn calls file quarantine the most restrictive DLP action for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: File quarantine is the most restrictive DLP action available for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Learn describes the quarantine site as containing highly sensitive files.
claims.quote: Because the quarantine site contains highly sensitive files

claims.claim: The Learn workflow describes automatic action on a match and no approval step.
claims.quote: Searched: DLP SharePoint OneDrive file quarantine restore automated approval audit operation quarantine. Opened learn, get-started and create-policy quarantine pages; their match workflow contains no approval step.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: All quarantined-file restore is manual and administrators decide when and whether to restore.
claims.quote: There's no automated file restore for quarantined files. All file restore is a manual process. Administrators decide when and whether to restore a quarantined file.

claims.claim: There is no quarantined-file restore action in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: There's no restore action available in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Original sharing permissions are not restored and the owner or administrator must reconfigure them.
claims.quote: Original sharing permissions aren't restored. The file owner or admin must reconfigure sharing permissions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Only the latest file version is restored.
claims.quote: Only the latest file version is restored. Previous versions aren't preserved through the quarantine and restore process.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions, Change & support
claims.claim: The same rule does not re-quarantine a restored file even after file or rule modification.
claims.quote: The same DLP rule won't re-quarantine the restored file, even if the file is modified or the policy rule is updated.

claims.claim: Other DLP rules continue to apply to a restored file.
claims.quote: Other DLP rules continue to apply normally to the restored file.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Quarantine may process a maximum of 200,000 items per tenant in a 24-hour period.
claims.quote: A maximum of 200,000 items per tenant within a 24-hour period may be processed for quarantine.

claims.claim: Items exceeding the processing limit may be processed later.
claims.quote: Items exceeding this limit may be processed at a later time.

claims.claim: Quarantine may not complete for file paths longer than 350 characters.
claims.quote: File quarantine may not be completed for files with file path lengths greater than 350 characters.

claims.claim: In the documented long-path failure case no tombstone is created and the quarantine action is not applied.
claims.quote: In such cases, the tombstone file will not be created, resulting in the quarantine action not being applied.

claims.claim: The quarantine destination must be a SharePoint site in the tenant and cannot be a subsite.
claims.quote: The quarantine destination must be a SharePoint site in your tenant. You can't use a subsite or a OneDrive location.

claims.claim: A OneDrive location cannot be the quarantine destination.
claims.quote: You can't use a subsite or a OneDrive location.

claims.claim: Selecting a subsite moves quarantined files to its containing site instead.
claims.quote: If you select a subsite, quarantined files are moved to the site that contains the subsite instead.

claims.claim: Any SharePoint site template can be used for quarantine.
claims.quote: You can use any SharePoint site template.

claims.claim: Quarantine supports all file types supported by DLP for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: File quarantine supports all file types that DLP supports for SharePoint and OneDrive locations.

claims.claim: Quarantine is not available as an on-demand classification action.
claims.quote: The quarantine action is not available as an on-demand classification action.

claims.claim: An on-demand scan classification can trigger quarantine when it matches a policy rule for the first time.
claims.quote: files that are scanned and classified by an on-demand scan can trigger the quarantine action if the classification result matches a DLP policy rule for the first time.

claims.claim: The quarantine folder path and tombstone message must be configured before selecting the policy action.
claims.quote: Before you can select the quarantine action in a DLP policy, you must configure the quarantine folder path and tombstone file message in DLP settings.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP auto-quarantine is a separate feature for files on Windows and macOS devices.
claims.quote:
DLP file quarantine for SharePoint and OneDrive is separate from these related features:
- Endpoint DLP auto-quarantine — Applies only to files on Windows and macOS devices.

claims.claim: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps file quarantine is a separate quarantine capability.
claims.quote: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps file quarantine — A similar quarantine capability that exists in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps (MDA).

claims.claim: Administrators are responsible for quarantine-site access control and lifecycle management.
claims.quote: Administrators are responsible for access control and lifecycle management of the quarantine site.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to use a dedicated quarantine site without active business content.
claims.quote: Don't use a site that contains active business content. Create a dedicated site for quarantine purposes.

claims.quote: Move the file from the quarantine site back to the original location.

claims.claim: Manual restore includes deleting the tombstone at the original location.

claims.claim: The printed Purview policy wizard path reaches Create rule, with the quarantine action supplied in the note.
claims.quote:
Select + Create rule. Name the rule and provide a description.
Under Actions, select Add an action > Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365 locations.
Select Block everyone and move file to quarantine location.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom policy > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > Actions > Add an action > Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365 locations > Block everyone and move file to quarantine location', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-quarantine. Its current endpoint is the correct rule page but not the action itself.
